audio_caption: The audio clip begins with one male speaker announcing that the song for the day is "Stitches by Shawn Mendes". Another male speaker responds in a casual, conversational tone, stating "we're going to start with the song structure" to "break down the different parts". The first speaker follows, stating "we've got a verse, pre-chorus, chorus, then another verse" and outlines the standard structure of the song. The second speaker replies, saying "this is about the most basic song structure you can get" and notes that it is the most popular song structure used today.

The audio clip begins with someone explaining how a song can be broken down into four guitar parts, "verse, pre-chorus, chorus and bridge", using the same four chords but in different orders. They then promote checking out a link with lyrics, chords, and other information. The speaker encourages listeners to tune their guitar and follow along, then asks for likes and comments for motivation to create more videos. The clip is spoken in an enthusiastic, instructional tone. Overall, the clip features one male speaker.

The audio clip begins with speech, a male speaker suggests "make sure to hit the subscribe button," encouraging access to new content. Shortly after, there's music, likely indie folk, with a somber mood, featuring acoustic guitar as the main instrument.

The guitar then plays again, performing this rhythm along with the speaker's instructions. The song continues with guitar playing the described rhythm and chords.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker introducing a segment focusing on the "pre-chorus". He announces a chord progression, then plays the chords on what sounds like an acoustic guitar. The chords are "F", "G", "A minor", and "G".

The clip begins with a single male speaker explaining a musical rhythm, describing counting beats and playing on specific ones. He uses a clear, instructional tone. Afterward, the sound shifts to music, specifically a strummed acoustic guitar playing what sounds like a chord progression. The music is relatively simple and has a slightly melancholic mood. Finally, there's another short burst of strummed guitar music.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker introducing a musical section, mentioning "the chorus" and referring back to a previous "verse". He then describes the chord progression, naming specific chords. He analyzes the rhythm and timing by counting out beats. Following his instructions, a guitar plays the chord progression he described, exhibiting a calm and instructional mood, likely meant as a tutorial or demonstration. Towards the end, strumming becomes more evident.

The clip begins with a male speaker stating, "Now finally, the bridge." The speaker then describes that the chord progression for the bridge is the same as the verse and chorus: "A minor, G, C, F." He goes on to explain the palm-muting technique, including placing the palm against the bridge of the guitar for a partially muted effect. He emphasizes the sound is not "entirely muted," nor "totally open," demonstrating a partially muted sound. The speaker says that the palm-muting on the beat and the end gives "an interesting sound" and is a common technique. He goes on to play the bridge with the plam-muting technique. He explains that it may take a little bit to get the hang of the plam-muting technique. The speaker ends by saying that if you play those four parts, you can play the entire song and then asks, "Did you like this video?"

The audio begins with a male speaker instructing the listener to subscribe to his YouTube channel, highlighting that doing so would provide immediate access to his newest content. He then points the listener to either of two other videos, encouraging them to embark on their next guitar adventure. The speaking tone is upbeat and energetic.
